title: Is Vienna Game a true story? The real Congress of Vienna behind it
answer: Partly. Hulu's "Vienna Game," out Nov. 18, 2026, is a satirical drama set at the real Congress of Vienna of 1814-15, and its heroine is based on a real noblewoman, Wilhelmine, Duchess of Sagan. But it is a satire with dramatized plot lines, not a documentary account.
body:
The six-part German series follows Wilhelmine von Sagan (Marlene Tanczik) through diplomacy, espionage and betrayal, and her affair with Baron Laski (Daniel Donskoy), a Bonapartist and political enemy. Disney calls the setting "the most opulent party of the 19th century." Hannu Salonen directed it from scripts by Stefan Brunner. In the U.S., all six episodes stream on Hulu from Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in German with subtitles.

The history is real. After Napoleon's defeat, European powers met in Vienna in 1814-15 to redraw the map, with Austrian Foreign Minister Klemens von Metternich leading talks aimed at a balance of power among Austria, Prussia, Russia, Britain and France. The real Wilhelmine (1781-1839) ran a salon attended by top nobility and had an affair with Metternich that began in 1813; more than 600 of his letters to her were found in 1949. During the Congress their affair ended, and her renewed romance with Prince Alfred of Windisch-Grätz distracted Metternich at a critical stage of the talks. Sources on the show do not identify Baron Laski as a historical figure.
in_the_news: "Vienna Game" premieres on Hulu on Nov. 18, 2026; it streams on Disney+ in other countries.

faq.q: Is Wilhelmine von Sagan a real person?
faq.a: Yes. Wilhelmine, Duchess of Sagan, lived from 1781 to 1839 and was Metternich's lover before and during the Congress of Vienna.

faq.q: What was the Congress of Vienna?
faq.a: A 1814-15 meeting of European powers, led by Austria's Metternich, to reorganize Europe after Napoleon's wars.
